paper_metadata.title: A simple variational quantum Monte Carlo-effective mass approach for excitons and trions in quantum dots

experiments.description: Variational quantum Monte Carlo with effective-mass Hamiltonian for a neutral exciton in a CdSe nanoplatelet, optimized with a Newton-Raphson loop over a single Jastrow parameter.

algorithm.variant: Variational Quantum Monte Carlo (VQMC) with Newton-Raphson optimization
algorithm.ansatz: Slater-Jastrow trial wave function with particle-in-box single-particle states and exponential Jastrow factor
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Iterate until convergence in energy or variational-parameter distance; paper mentions an energy convergence threshold of about 1 meV in the benchmark runs

hyperparameters.thermalization: included at start of random walk
hyperparameters.NPL_dimensions: (Lx, Ly, Lz) = (30, 10, 1.4) nm for the main benchmark
hyperparameters.basis_state_form: Phi_i = cos(kx xi) cos(ky yi) cos(kz zi)

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial guess M0 provided as input; arbitrary initial random-walk step size r0 chosen and then thermally adjusted to target acceptance

optimizer_settings.tolerance: energy threshold about 1 meV in reported benchmarks

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Continuous-space effective-mass model; no qubit encoding
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize the variational expectation value of the exciton Hamiltonian H_X = sum_i (p_i^2 / 2m_i + V_i) + V_c(re,rh) + Egap
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Hard-wall confinement through infinite potential outside the nanoplatelet; dielectric confinement included via self-energy and polarization Coulomb terms

problem_instance.description: Ground-state neutral exciton in colloidal CdSe nanoplatelets with strong dielectric confinement

dataset_specification.description: CdSe nanoplatelet model; benchmark geometry (30, 10, 1.4) nm; comparison against full variational calculation from Ref. [8]

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: No dataset preprocessing; material parameters and geometry are supplied directly
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Energy evaluated as a function of alpha for different walker counts; compared against exact/full variational results

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Set effective masses, dielectric constants, band gap, nanoplatelet dimensions, and initial variational parameter; generate multiple random walkers; thermalize step size to target ~50% acceptance
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Average local energies over walkers; Newton-Raphson update of alpha; compare against exact variational reference
implementation_details.total_execution_time: few minutes for convergence in reported benchmarks

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: Energy vs alpha shows a clear minimum around alpha ≈ 0.72
convergence_data.variance_across_runs: Reported dependence on number of walkers and points per walker; accuracy improves from N = 10^7 to N = 10^9

speedup_claims.conditions: Accuracy and computational efficiency comparison for CdSe nanoplatelet exciton benchmark
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper claims VQMC matches the exact/full variational result and is computationally efficient, but does not quantify a formal speedup factor for this specific benchmark.

experiments.description: Variational quantum Monte Carlo with effective-mass Hamiltonian for a positive trion in a CdSe nanoplatelet, optimized over three variational parameters.

algorithm.variant: Variational Quantum Monte Carlo (VQMC) with Newton-Raphson optimization for trion
algorithm.ansatz: Slater-Jastrow trial wave function with two electron-hole cusp factors and one Padé Jastrow factor for hole-hole correlation
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Iterate until convergence in energy or variational-parameter distance; benchmarked with about 1 meV energy convergence threshold

hyperparameters.thermalization: included at start of random walk
hyperparameters.NPL_dimensions: (Lx, Ly, Lz) = (30, 10, 1.4) nm for the main benchmark
hyperparameters.dielectric_constants: epsilon_in = 6, epsilon_out varied from 2 to epsilon_in
hyperparameters.basis_state_form: Phi_i = cos(kx xi) cos(ky yi) cos(kz zi)
hyperparameters.Jastrow_form: exp(-Z r1) exp(-Z r2) exp(b r12 / (1 + a r12))

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial guess M0 provided as input; arbitrary initial random-walk step size r0 chosen and then thermally adjusted to target acceptance

optimizer_settings.tolerance: energy threshold about 1 meV in reported benchmarks

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Continuous-space effective-mass model; no qubit encoding
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize the variational expectation value of the trion Hamiltonian H_X+ = sum_i (p_i^2 / 2m_i + V_i) + Vc(re,rh1) + Vc(re,rh2) + Vc(rh1,rh2) + Egap
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Hard-wall confinement through infinite potential outside the nanoplatelet; dielectric confinement included via self-energy and polarization Coulomb terms
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_X+ = sum_{i=e,h1,h2} (p_i^2 / 2m_i + V_i) + Vc(re,rh1) + Vc(re,rh2) + Vc(rh1,rh2) + Egap

problem_instance.description: Ground-state positive trion in colloidal CdSe nanoplatelets with strong dielectric confinement; dielectric mismatch sweep from epsilon_out = 2 to epsilon_out = epsilon_in

dataset_specification.description: CdSe nanoplatelet model; benchmark geometry (30, 10, 1.4) nm; comparison against CI with 12 and 24 spin-orbital basis sets and against exciton binding energy reference

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: No dataset preprocessing; material parameters and geometry are supplied directly
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Energy and binding energy evaluated as a function of outer dielectric constant; compared against CI baselines and exciton reference

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Set effective masses, dielectric constants, band gap, nanoplatelet dimensions, and initial variational parameters; generate multiple random walkers; thermalize step size to target ~50% acceptance
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Average local energies over walkers; Newton-Raphson update of zeta, beta, alpha; compare against CI and full variational references
implementation_details.total_execution_time: few minutes for convergence in reported benchmarks

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: Energy and binding energy vary smoothly with dielectric mismatch; trion energy shift is more pronounced than exciton
convergence_data.variance_across_runs: Reported dependence on number of walkers and points per walker; execution time increases by about 1.5x relative to exciton

speedup_claims.conditions: Comparison of trion energies and binding energies in CdSe nanoplatelets
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper states VQMC is more accurate and computationally efficient, but does not provide a formal numerical speedup factor versus CI for the trion benchmark.
